study.title: Acupuncture mobilizes the brain's default mode and its anti-correlated network in healthy subjects
study.study_design: Within-subject experimental fMRI study with multiple acupuncture conditions and tactile stimulation comparison in healthy volunteers
study.randomization: Acupoints administered in randomized order on each subject
study.blinding: Participants were blinded to the study conditions; told acupuncture was to be performed at different acupuncture points using different techniques
study.exclusion_criteria: Neurological, mental and medical disorders, drug abuse, history of head trauma with loss of consciousness, and contraindications for exposure to high magnetic field

extraction_notes.note: Table 1 structure is complex with paired columns for acupuncture and tactile stimulation and a third column for paired t-test p-values. Some rows in the tactile column show 'nil' (no significant result). Coordinates extracted represent the acupuncture column peak voxels. The t* values in Table 1 represent peak voxel values from the acupuncture condition compared to baseline (needle in place); the paired t-test p-values represent comparison between acupuncture and tactile stimulation. These have been preserved separately as contrast CON_GLM_acu_vs_tactile_deact and CON_GLM_acu_vs_tactile_act.
The subgenual cingulate (L, BA32/24) acupuncture coordinates in Table 1 appear to list x=-5 but the printed table column shows '-5' in an unclear OCR context. Transcribed as printed.

% signal change values for the peak voxels in the deactivation and activation network comparisons from Table 1 were extracted as reported but the column headers describing the exact signal change metric label (t* vs. % signal change) are potentially ambiguous from OCR. The paper states: 'The mean % change in the signal intensity of the peak voxels and the variations (t values) between the datasets are presented for the structures of each group.' The two numeric columns appear to be t* (t-value at peak voxel) and % signal change.

Table 2 deqi column percent signal change (% of volume) was listed in the original table but OCR extraction was partial. Individual % volume values for Table 2 structures were not fully resolvable and have been omitted from coordinate entries to avoid hallucination.

The paper reports that n=48 subjects were analyzed for the main acupuncture analysis, but comparisons with tactile stimulation were made on n=37 subjects. The deqi vs. mixed pain comparison used 52 scans in 37 subjects (deqi) and 52 scans in 29 subjects (mixed). These different Ns have been preserved in individual contrast entries.

Figures 1, 2, 3, 5, and 6 contain neuroimaging results but exact coordinates cannot be read from figure captions or text. Only narrative descriptions are available for those results not also reported in Tables 1 or 2.

CCA results in Figures 4.1 and 4.2 show seed-based correlations with labelled brain regions but specific cluster coordinates are not tabulated. The reference voxel coordinates are extracted from figure captions. Individual correlation strengths (z-values, r-values) are not explicitly reported in numeric form.

No formal expectancy or credibility scale was administered. The only blinding measure described is the participant being told that different acupuncture techniques were being performed. No expectancy rating data are reported.

The paper references a previous detailed psychophysical report for 42 of the 48 subjects (Hui et al., 2007). Individual deqi subscale scores (e.g., numerical ratings for aching, soreness, etc.) are not reported in this paper.

The tactile stimulation condition is described as 'not an inert control but as a means to help understand how acupuncture compares with a conventional form of sensory stimulation' and also 'can be regarded as a form of sham acupuncture.' This dual characterization means the arm is classified as active_control but this should be noted for review.
Coordinate space is explicitly stated as Talairach space throughout. No MNI coordinates are reported.

Individual acupoint sample sizes differ: LI4 = 37 subjects/64 scans, ST36 = 43 subjects/73 scans, LV3 = 37 subjects/64 scans. The 48-subject combined analysis merges these overlapping subject groups. This overlap structure means the combined n=48 is not a simple sum.
No clinical outcome measures (pain scales, symptom scores, quality of life) were administered. This is a pure neuroimaging study in healthy volunteers.

Table 1 contains multiple columns and the OCR rendering across pages 35-37 was partially fragmented. Values have been cross-referenced against table captions and text descriptions. Some p-values in Table 1 appear only in the right-most paired t-test column and may not apply individually to all rows listed.
The paper does not report conflict of interest disclosures.
